title: Homemade Ramen
excerpt: First ramen attempt: broth, noodles, and what I learned.
content:
My Ramen Challenge: From Scratch

　I've always wanted to try making authentic ramen, and this time I went all in—crafting everything from the broth to the noodles myself. Here is the story of my culinary journey to create this special bowl.


The Broth: Soul of the Ramen

　The foundation of any good ramen is its broth. I let chicken bones and garlic simmer for hours, carefully drawing out the rich, deep flavors. The wonderful aroma filled the house and built up the anticipation.


Custom Noodles and "Tare" Seasoning

　For the noodles, I wanted a personal touch, kneading a special dough with chives, garlic, and egg. The "tare" (the seasoning base) that defines the soup's final character was made from soy sauce infused with kombu (kelp). Combining this with the broth right before serving is the key to a fragrant and flavorful result.


The Final Bowl: A Taste of Accomplishment

　Finally, all the elements came together into my very own, unique bowl of ramen. The more time and effort you invest, the more personal and special the flavor becomes. I believe this sense of accomplishment is the best spice for any homemade dish.


Epilogue: Now It's Your Turn!

　You can adapt the toppings and seasonings using delicious ingredients from your own country. If this inspires you, I highly recommend giving it a try—the process itself is just as rewarding as the meal! For detailed instructions on how to make the noodles from scratch, please see the recipe on the Cooking page.
